title: eludite.debug.start input
description: Debug > Start Debugging (F5) or Start Without Debugging (Ctrl+F5): build the startup project first (when the setting build.beforeRun is on, the default: eludite.build.project's build, streamed to the Output window) and, when the build succeeds, run its built program with its launchSettings.json profile's arguments and environment, with or without debugging (Ctrl+F5: its output in the Output window's Debug source). The adapter follows the project's target framework and the platform: a .NET (Core) project (`netcoreapp*`, `net5.0` and later) runs as `dotnet <dll>` under netcoredbg; a .NET Framework project (`net2*` to `net4*`, or a legacy project's TargetFrameworkVersion v2.0 to v4.8.1) runs on Linux and macOS as `mono <exe>` under eludite-dbg-mono (the Mono soft-debugger adapter, protocol/schemas/dap-mono.md) with the located Mono (setting debugger.monoPrefix), and on Windows is refused with a message until eludite-dbg-netfx (brief 0004) exists; Ctrl+F5 runs the .exe directly there. A Cargo package (a member of the open folder's Cargo workspace, named by its package name or its Cargo.toml) builds through the Cargo build path (`cargo build -p <package>`, `--release` in the Release configuration) and runs its binary target (`target/debug/<name>`, or `target/release/<name>`) on every platform under lldb-dap, LLVM's LLDB debug adapter located on the machine (setting debugger.lldbDapPath; protocol/schemas/dap-lldb.md), with the Rust toolchain's LLDB formatters loaded (setting debugger.rustFormatters); `session.runtime` is `native`. Its arguments and environment come from `[package.metadata.eludite.run]` in its Cargo.toml (`args`, a list; `env`, a table); it runs in the workspace root, as `cargo run` does; Ctrl+F5 runs the executable. With `test`, the package's test executable is built (`cargo test --no-run -p <package>`) and debugged with `args` as the test filter and `--nocapture`, as `cargo test` passes them. A failed or canceled build does not launch: the Error List comes forward and the status bar says why. Refused while a session is running or building (use eludite.debug.continue to resume a break). The answer is the stop summary (debug-stop-summary.output.json): where and why it stopped, the top frames, the top frame's locals and the watches within the budget parameters, and the program's output since `output_since`; on a timeout `mode` is `running` (or `launching`, `building`), and after the session ends `design` with `exit_code` and `message`.
x-eludite-escalates: Dangerous when the solution's policy sets `debug.drive` to `prompt`; refused for agents when it sets `debug.drive` to `deny`.

project.description: The project to run: its path (absolute or relative to the solution folder) or its name as the Workspace window shows it. Default: the startup project (eludite.workspace.set_startup_project), else the solution's first executable project.

debug.description: False runs without the debugger (Ctrl+F5). Default true.

profile.description: The launchSettings.json profile to use. Default: the first profile whose commandName is Project.

build.description: Build the project before launching. Default: the setting build.beforeRun (true unless changed).

target.description: A Cargo package's binary target to run, by name, when the package has several (default: its only binary; with several and none named the start is refused, listing them). With `test`: the test target whose executable to debug (default: the library's unit tests, else the only binary's). Cargo packages only.

test.description: Debug the Cargo package's test executable instead of its binary: build it with `cargo test --no-run --message-format=json -p <package>` (its compiler-artifact message names the executable) and run it with `args` and `--nocapture`. Default false. Cargo packages only.

args.description: The program's arguments, instead of `[package.metadata.eludite.run]`'s `args`; with `test`, the test harness's arguments: a test-name filter (`my_test`), `--exact`, `--ignored` (Eludite adds `--nocapture`). Cargo packages only: a .NET project's come from its launchSettings.json profile.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for the debuggee to break, exit or settle before answering, in milliseconds. From the UI the command never waits; from another thread (an agent) the default is 5000. A build before the launch counts against it: an answer with mode `building` or `launching` means the session is still starting; call eludite.debug.wait or eludite.debug.snapshot later.

depth.description: How many levels of the locals to expand: 1 (default) lists the top level only; up to 5. Expansion is breadth-first and stops when `max_variables` rows are listed.

max_variables.description: The most variable rows listed, counting every level (default 50, at most 500).

max_value_chars.description: Values longer than this are cut and end with `… (N chars)`, the row saying `value_truncated` (default 200, at most 10000).

max_frames.description: The most stack frames listed (default 10, at most 200); page further with eludite.debug.stack.

max_output_lines.description: The most program output lines listed (default 20, at most 1000; 0 lists none).

output_since.description: An output cursor (`output.next` of an earlier answer, or eludite.debug.output's `next`): list the program's lines from it on. Default: the last `max_output_lines` lines.
